(born February 11, 1993) is an American basketball player who played his [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Kansas]]. McLemore is known for his athletic ability complemented by his outstanding jump shot. His size, style of play and unique set of abilities have garnered comparisons to NBA sharpshooter [[Ray Allen]].{{cite web|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1491949-nba-draft-breakdown-and-projections-for-kansas-star-ben-mclemore |title=NBA Draft Breakdown and Projections for Kansas Star Ben McLemore |publisher=Bleacher Report |date=2013-01-19 |accessdate=2013-03-08}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/could-kansas-ben-mclemore-go-1 |title=Could Kansas' Ben McLemore Go #1? |publisher=NBADraft.net |date=2012-12-26 |accessdate=2013-03-08}}{{cite web|url=http://nbadraft.net/players/ben-mclemore |title=Ben McLemore |publisher=NBADraft.net |date= |accessdate=2013-03-08}} He is considered one of the top prospects for the [[2013 NBA Draft]].[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Ben-McLemore-6258/ NBA Draft Prospect of the Week: Ben McLemore]. Draft Express (December 24, 2012). Retrieved on 2013-01-11.[http://nbadraft.net/players/ben-mclemore 23 – Ben McLemore]. NBA Draft.net. Retrieved on 2013-01-11. McLemore declared for the NBA Draft on April 9, 2013. ==Early life== McLemore was born in [[St. Louis, Missouri]] to parents Ben McLemore II and Sonya Reid. He is the fourth of five children. ==High school career== McLemore played [[high school basketball]] at Wellston High School in [[St. Louis, Missouri]] for three years, before his school was shut down in 2010. He then attended both [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]] and [[Christian Life Center Academy (Humble, Texas)|Christian Life Centre]] in [[Humble, Texas]] during his senior year of high school. On the national scale, McLemore was ranked No. 17 overall and No. 4 among shooting guards by Rivals.com at the conclusion of his high school career. ==College career== After committing to Kansas, McLemore was deemed ineligible to play by the NCAA. This was due to the fact that he attended multiple high schools, resulting in his transcripts being "a little fuzzy."{{cite web|last=Keeley |first=Sean |url=http://www.sbnation.com/ncaa-basketball/2011/10/14/2491002/kansas-freshmen-ben-mclemore-jamari-traylor-ineligible |title=Kansas Declares Freshmen Ben McLemore, Jamari Traylor Ineligible |publisher=SBNation.com |date=2011-10-14 |accessdate=2013-03-08}} He was allowed to practice with the team and take part in team activities starting in the 2nd semester of the school year.{{cite web|last=Bedore |first=Gary |url=http://www2.ljworld.com/news/2011/oct/14/ku-freshmen-ben-mclemore-jamari-traylor-ineligible/ |title=KU freshmen Ben McLemore, Jamari Traylor ineligible for 2011-12 season / LJWorld.com |publisher=.ljworld.com |date= |accessdate=2013-03-08}} At the beginning of his college career, McLemore was considered to be either a late first round or early second round prospect.
